ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A positive point charge with a charge of $2\times10^{-8}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from infinity to point A in an electric field, requiring work of $2\times10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$ to overcome the electric field force. If the charge is moved from point B in the electric field to infinity, the work done by the electric field force is $8\times10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$. The potential at infinity is taken to be zero.

1. Find the electric potential at point A.
2. Find the potential difference between points A and B.
3. The work done in moving a negative charge of $2\times10^{-5}\mathrm{C}$ from point A to point B.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A positive point charge with a charge of $2\times10^{-8}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from infinity to point A in an electric field, requiring work of $2\times10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$ to overcome the electric field force. If the charge is moved from point B in the electric field to infinity, the work done by the electric field force is $8\times10^{-6}\mathrm{J}$. The potential at infinity is taken to be zero. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem is a purely textual electric-potential calculation and does not require image evidence. Take the potential at infinity as V_∞=0. Given the positive test charge q=2×10^-8 C. 1. When moving from infinity to A, an external force is required to do work W_ext=2×10^-6 J against the electric field force. According to the change in electric potential energy, during quasi-static movement W_ext=ΔU=q(V_A−V_∞). Therefore V_A=(2×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=100 V. 2. When the same positive charge moves from B to infinity, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=8×10^-6 J. The formula for work done by the electric field force is W_field=q(V_initial−V_final)=q(V_B−V_∞). Therefore V_B=(8×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=400 V. The potential difference between A and B asked for in the problem is taken according to the method as V_A−V_B=100−400=−300 V. 3. For the negative charge q'=-2×10^-5 C, from A to B, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=q'(V_A−V_B)=(-2×10^-5)×(-300)=6×10^-3 J.

1. When moving from infinity to A, an external force is required to do work W_ext=2×10^-6 J against the electric field force. According to the change in electric potential energy, during quasi-static movement W_ext=ΔU=q(V_A−V_∞). Therefore V_A=(2×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=100 V.

2. When the same positive charge moves from B to infinity, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=8×10^-6 J. The formula for work done by the electric field force is W_field=q(V_initial−V_final)=q(V_B−V_∞). Therefore V_B=(8×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=400 V. The potential difference between A and B asked for in the problem is taken according to the method as V_A−V_B=100−400=−300 V.

3. For the negative charge q'=-2×10^-5 C, from A to B, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=q'(V_A−V_B)=(-2×10^-5)×(-300)=6×10^-3 J.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
The problem is a purely textual electric-potential calculation and does not require image evidence. Take the potential at infinity as V_∞=0. Given the positive test charge q=2×10^-8 C.

1. When moving from infinity to A, an external force is required to do work W_ext=2×10^-6 J against the electric field force. According to the change in electric potential energy, during quasi-static movement W_ext=ΔU=q(V_A−V_∞). Therefore V_A=(2×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=100 V.

2. When the same positive charge moves from B to infinity, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=8×10^-6 J. The formula for work done by the electric field force is W_field=q(V_initial−V_final)=q(V_B−V_∞). Therefore V_B=(8×10^-6)/(2×10^-8)=400 V. The potential difference between A and B asked for in the problem is taken according to the method as V_A−V_B=100−400=−300 V.

3. For the negative charge q'=-2×10^-5 C, from A to B, the work done by the electric field force is W_field=q'(V_A−V_B)=(-2×10^-5)×(-300)=6×10^-3 J.
